the_line: Lean proves that a conclusion follows from stated premises. It does not adjudicate reality. Every theorem in this repo is of the form 'if these premises hold, then this follows', and a kernel proof of it is silent on whether any organism satisfies the premises. So a grand question has a formalisable core exactly to the extent that part of the disagreement about it is a disagreement about what follows from what, and an empirical remainder exactly to the extent that it is a disagreement about what the world is like. Most of these questions are mostly remainder. Two of them (the Price equation, Hamilton's rule) are disputes in which the formal part has been repeatedly confused with the empirical part for decades, and those are the ones where formalisation would do the most good. A capability map that let the first kind of progress be read as the second would be worse than no map.
name: Fisher's fundamental theorem and its interpretation
question: Does natural selection increase mean fitness at a rate equal to the additive genetic variance in fitness, and if so, under what conditions and in what sense?
dispute: Fisher 1930 stated it as having 'the supreme position among the biological sciences'; Price 1972 made clear it concerns only the partial change due to allele-frequency change in a constant environment; Ewens 1989 and Ewens and Lessard 2015 gave the standard modern reading; Grafen 2018 offered a third; Basener and Sanford 2018 claimed it fails with mutation and Hancock and Cardinale 2024 replied directly. Every one of those positions is a claim about which premises the theorem needs, which is why this question's formalisable core is unusually large.

statements.claim: If a haploid population has frequency vector p and constant fitnesses w, then after selection the change in mean fitness equals the variance of w under p divided by the mean of w.
statements.settles: The theorem under its narrowest honest reading. It is proved here, and what it establishes is a consequence of constant fitnesses and a finite type, not a fact about any population.

statements.claim: Under the same premises, mean fitness is non-decreasing; and therefore a claimed DECLINE in mean fitness under constant fitnesses and no mutation is impossible.
statements.settles: The elimination form: a claimed trajectory of mean fitness that falls, with the premises stated, is ruled out. The repo proves the elimination separately from the equality.

statements.claim: If the additive genetic variance in fitness is zero, then the change in mean fitness is zero, so a claimed change under zero variance is impossible.
statements.settles: The degenerate case, proved separately, which is where overstated readings of the theorem break first.

statements.claim: If mutation is added with a stated rate and a stated effect distribution, then the change in mean fitness is NOT in general equal to the additive variance over the mean, and the conditions under which the equality survives are determined.
statements.settles: The Basener-Sanford dispute's formal half: whether the theorem's scope extends to mutation-selection balance. It is a question about premises, and a formalisation would make each side's premises explicit instead of arguable.

items.what: Whether mean fitness actually increases in any real population over any real interval.
items.why_not_provable: The theorem is silent on this, and the commonest misreading of it is to treat the proof as the answer.
items.measurement: Longitudinal fitness measurement in a population with a stable definition of fitness, which is itself contested.

items.what: Whether the environment is constant, which the narrow form requires and which is almost never true.
items.why_not_provable: An empirical property of the population's circumstances.
items.measurement: Measurement of fitness-relevant environmental variation over the same interval as the fitness measurement.

items.what: Whether the additive approximation to the genetic variance is adequate for the trait in question.
items.why_not_provable: Depends on the actual genetic architecture.
items.measurement: Variance decomposition from a breeding design or a mutant panel.

items.what: What the actual mutation rate and effect distribution are, which decides whether the mutation-selection extension matters in practice.
items.why_not_provable: Both are measurements of a particular organism in a particular environment.

in_repo.note: The theorem, an alternative form, monotonicity, and a proof that selection preserves the frequency simplex, so the statement is not vacuous on a degenerate input.
Three elimination forms, so the theorem can be used to rule out a claim and not only to assert one.
In the registry with its scope, its named hypotheses and its non-vacuity witness, reachable from the MCP tools, both CLIs and the static mirror.

tools_needed.name: lean_law_get
tools_needed.note: The theorem's Lean source, premises, scope and witness, which is what makes the narrowness of the claim visible.

tools_needed.name: lean_propose
tools_needed.note: The route for the mutation-selection extension, which would enter as a new law rather than as a new version of this one.

tools_needed.name: premise_check
tools_needed.note: To settle the published dispute one would need to formalise each side's stated premises and check which conclusions follow. Nothing extracts premises from a paper.

tools_needed.name: teach_claim
tools_needed.note: This is the single best teaching example of the formalisable/empirical line, and there is no tool that packages it as one.

scope: This is a map of what is formalisable, not a research programme and not a claim that the formalisable parts are the important parts. The (a)/(b) split is a judgement made here and is arguable for every entry; where it is contentious the dispute field says so. The list is not exhaust: there is no canonical set of grand questions in biology, and this one is weighted toward evolution, development and scaling because that is what this project reads. Several entries have no counterpart in open-problems/problems.json, which is a gap in that enumeration rather than evidence the question is settled. Nothing here is about the held-out exam clade.
